title: Student notes: tide mills
bodyMd:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes.

- A tide mill is a watermill driven by the rise and fall of the tide rather than by a river's current.
- The incoming tide fills a pond behind a dam; a gate closes when the tide is at its highest.
- As the sea falls away outside the dam, water let out of the pond turns the mill wheel.
- A tide mill can grind only while its pond is emptying, so its working hours move about fifty minutes later each day.
- The restored tide mill at Cleave Point, Devon, grinds flour for two hours on each falling tide.
- Miller Rhona Dell says customers have to consult a tide table to find out when the mill will be open.
accessibilityText: A list of six research notes taken by a student about tide mills. One: a tide mill is a watermill driven by the rise and fall of the tide rather than by a river's current. Two: the incoming tide fills a pond behind a dam, and a gate closes when the tide is at its highest. Three: as the sea falls away outside the dam, water let out of the pond turns the mill wheel. Four: a tide mill can grind only while its pond is emptying, so its working hours move about fifty minutes later each day. Five: the restored tide mill at Cleave Point, Devon, grinds flour for two hours on each falling tide. Six: miller Rhona Dell says customers have to consult a tide table to find out when the mill will be open.

provenance.notes: Original note set written for this item bank. The Cleave Point mill and the miller are invented; the description of how a tide mill works is general background and was not adapted from any source.
